newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-UNITED URGE FANS TO FLY THE FLAG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNITED URGE FANS TO FLY THE FLAG.

text.p: Manchester United, for so many years England's flag-bearers in European competition, are now asking their own fans to fly the flag for them when they face titleholders Juventus in their vital Champions League match at Old Trafford on Wednesday.

United surrendered their 40-year-long unbeaten home European record when they lost 1-0 to Fenerbahce of Turkey two weeks ago, and now United manager Alex Ferguson wants Old Trafford to regain some of its fearful imposing atmosphere of old.
"We've got to get Old Trafford back to being a cauldron of noise once again, a place where teams are afraid to come," said Ferguson on Monday.

"I want the fans to bring flags into the ground again and for them to help build up an intimidating atmosphere. When we lost to Fenerbahce the crowd was too quiet and they only really got going after Fenerbahce scored.
"Wednesday's game against Juventus is a very important one for us and I hope the tempo of our game will be much quicker and the crowd will respond and make it more like a European night of old."
United would have already secured their place in the last eight of the competition if they had beaten Fenerbahce at home, but their shock defeat has thrown their qualification into doubt.
Juventus, who beat United 1-0 in Turin in September, lead the Group C standings with 10 points -- four more than second-placed United, and need only a draw to guarantee their place in the last eight.

United ended a run of three successive defeats with a 1-0 win over Arsenal on Saturday and will be desperate not to lose at home for the second European match in a row. If they should, Fenerbahce seem more than capable of beating Rapid Vienna, who went down 5-0 to Juventus two weeks ago, and if that scenario was played out, the Turks would be favourites to qualify along with Juventus.
Juventus drew 0-0 with AC Milan in a Serie A match on Sunday night and despite the draw coach Marcello Lippi was pleased with his team's performance.
"I'm very satisfied with the way we played, " he said, "We came back from defeat by Inter well, we played good soccer for over an hour, giving very little away to our opponents."
Central defenders, Uruguyan Paolo Montero and Ciro Ferrara, both suspended against Milan, are expected to return against Manchester United, probably in place of Mark Juliano and Alessio Tacchinardi.

While Juventus should advance to the last eight, there is still some concern for Milan, who are second in Group D, six points behind leaders Porto, the only side in the champions league with a a 100 per cent record, and three points ahead of both Gothenburg and Rosenborg who meet in Norway.

Milan travel to Porto and if they drop three points as they did to the Portuguese at home, what was thought to be an effortless passage for them into the quarter-finals, could well depend on their last match at home to Rosenborg on December 4.

Milan's Uruguyan coach Oscar Tabarez was also pleased with his side after Sunday's draw with Juventus, saying: "Tonight I saw the real character of the side. Sure Juventus put us under pressure because Juventus are a good side but we reacted immediately, we got back into the game and came close to scoring."
Frenchman Marcel Desailly and Christian Panucci, who both missed the Turin game, may return in place of Dutchman Michael Reiziger and Stefano Eranio.
In-form Roberto Baggio seems certain to hold on to his place in attack alongside Liberian George Weah, while veteran captain Franco Baresi, influential against Juventus, again marshals the defence.

Porto, who won 3-2 in Milan, need only a draw at home to clinch first place in the group. The club shrugged off recent controversies to beat Rio Ave 1-0 away over the weekend to maintain their lead at the top of the league.

Dutch champions Ajax, who are having an erratic season at home, should virtually secure their place in the quarter-finals with a home win over Auxerre, whose coach Guy Roux admits his side now need a miracle to advance.

Grasshopper Zurich, who play Rangers in Glasgow, top Group A on goal difference from the Dutch side who should pick up three points against the French champions, a shadow of the team that won the league last season.
In the UEFA Cup, Italian league leaders Internazionale Milan hope to lay ghosts from the past to rest when they host Boavista of Portugal in the opening leg of their third round tie on Tuesday.

The last time these two teams met in this competition -- in the 1991-92 season -- Inter were the defending champions, and they travelled to Portugal for the first leg of their first round tie in confident mood.
But they lost 2-1 and were then held at home 0-0 to go out of the Cup at the first hurdle.
Current form suggests the Italians should find things a little easier this time round in their bid to win the trophy for the third time in seven years.
